full_judgment:
Mr. A.K.M. Shahidul Huq J :- This Rule on an application filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the proceeding GR No.5405/97 arising out of Sutrapur Police Station Case No.75 (10) 97 now pending before the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, should not be quashed. 

 2. The short facts for disposal of the Rule is that one Mr. Azam Ali Talukder, Assistant Sub Inspector of Sutrapur Police Station, Dhaka lodged an ejahar with the Sutrpur Police Station on 16.10.97 at 21.5 hour, alleging, inter alia, that for Eviction of illegal occupant from the holding no 1/1 Chandra Mohon Basak lane and to-being the control of it as a Government property on 8/6/97 has been fixed under Memo No.1024 V.P. dated 1-6-97, the Police 'Commissioner (East) was requested for 1 officer and 15 police forces and for that purpose one Sub Inspector (Daroga) and one Platoon S.A.F was deployed. Then on 8/6/97 under the direction of Mr. Fazlul Hoq to Magistrate, class and Sub Inspector Mr. Moment)) Ahsan with the assistance of the police platoon, Eviction was done in 4(four) rooms in 1st Floor in the back side (North Portion) and illegal Occupant Zakir Hossain, son of Chan Mia, his mother and other family members found present and after evicting them the rooms were locked and sealed and handed over to the authority and since then the rooms are under the possession of Government and under the control of the signatory, Subsequently on secret information the informant went there and saw that a gate has been constructed by closing down entrance and that with the assistance of some persons entered into the house and found that the evicted persons were living there and they have been trying to grab the Government property and they have trespassed by the breaking the lock and started living constructing iron gate by breaking the wooden gate and thus they changed the nature of vested property and as such committed punishable offence. In this regard the concerned Lawyer gave opinion to file Criminal Case while he was asked for the opinion and prayed for taking action against Mr. Zakir Hossain, son of Chand Mia and others as per the provisions of law. 

 4. It is stated that the disputed holding No.1/1 Chandra Mohon Basak street is owned by Kazi Abdul Mattalib, son of Late Kazi Ahmed All and Mosammat Momtaj Begum, daughter of Mohammad Khadem All of 19, Larmini Street, Wari and have constructed multi-storied building there on and the accused petitioner No.2 is possessing the suit property under the plantiff as their Attorney. The Government illegally listed the property as a vested and non resident property under V.P. Case No.44 of 77 for which the title of Kazi Abdul Motaleb have been curbed and under the circumstance the said Motaleb and another instituted a suit for declaration before the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhakd through his Attorney, the petitioner No.2 being renumbered as Title Suit No.66 of 1088. 

 7. The further contentions of the petitioners are that the petitioners are in possession of the suit property and the order of statusquo is in favour of the petitioners despite of such order, the opposite party wanted to enter into the promises violating the order of statusquo thereby a violation Miscellaneous case is pending and again such criminal proceeding which is gross violation of law to a peace loving citizen, a harassment, a devise in a colourable manner, they wanted to occupy the premises as such the same is an abuse of the process of court and law which is required to be quashed. 

 9. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the proceeding of Sutrapur Police Station Case No.57(10) 1997 G.R. Case No.5405/97 under section 427 and 448 of the Penal Code now pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka the petitioner invoked the inherent jurisdiction of this Court as laid down under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the present Rule and also an order of stay all further proceeding of Sutrapur Police Station Case No.57(10) 1997 G.R. Case No.5405/97 now pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. 

 11. Mr. K.M. Zahid Sarwar, the learned Deputy Attorney General for the. State opposite party duly contesting the Rule submits that the FIR itself disclosed the offence against the petitioner under section 427/448 of the Penal Code and accordingly the proceeding cannot be quashed unless cognizance in respect thereof has been taken and process issued. In support of his contention he referred the decision in the case of Abdul Huque and others Vs the State reported in 60 DLR (AD) Page-01. 

 12. Heard the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the State Perused the application filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and other relevant papers and materials on records. In the instant case, cognizance has already been taken against the accused petitioner and since the cognizance has already been taken against the accused petitioner, so it cannot be taken so lightly and it must be dealt with seriously and without taking any evidence it is not possible to arrive at a correct findings over the matter in dispute. So in our view the application as filed by the petitioner under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal procedure is incompetent and premature and as such from the plain reading of the FIR we do not feel that it is a fit case for quashing and as such the application filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal procedure is not at all maintainable in the eye of law. 

 13. We find force in the submission of the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the State who rightly pointed out that before taking cognizance of the case by the competent court or tribunal the proceeding cannot be said to be pending and accordingly the proceeding cannot be quashed unless cognizance in respect thereof has been taken and process issued. In view of the submission of the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the State opposite party and the citation as referred above we are inclined to discharge the Rule as the very application filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not at all maintainable in the eye of law and the same is devoid of any substance. 

 15. The court of learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka is hereby directed to dispose of the G.R. Case No.5405/97 arising out of Sutrapur PS Case No.75(10)97 expeditiously preferably within 4(four) months from the date of receipt of this Judgment positively.
